args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
(Tracked-Changes Redline — Lender/Secured Party Markup of Counterparty Draft)

Document Status: COUNTERPARTY DRAFT WITH SECURED PARTY REQUIRED MODIFICATIONS
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
Prepared for: Internal Client Working Group / Credit Agreement Collateral Package
Governing Framework: UCC Article 9 (control of deposit accounts); executed Senior Secured Credit Agreement; Firm ACA Playbook; Depository Bank Standard Form; Account Schedule and related correspondence/checklists

Legend (tracked changes convention used in this text deliverable):
[DELETE: text] = counterparty language to be deleted
[INSERT: text] = secured-party required insertion or restoration
[RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: text] = firm-playbook / credit-agreement-required language reinstated over silent or off-market counterparty change
[COMMENT: …] = drafting note to negotiating counsel (not contractual text)

================================================================================
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
================================================================================

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"), dated as of [________ __], 20[__] (the "Effective Date"), is entered into by and among:

(i) [DEBTOR LEGAL NAME], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Debtor");
(ii) [ADMINISTRATIVE AGENT / COLLATERAL AGENT LEGAL NAME], as [Administrative Agent / Collateral Agent] for the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement referred to below (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns, the "Secured Party"); and
(iii) [DEPOSITORY BANK LEGAL NAME] (the "Bank").

[COMMENT: Confirm party block matches Credit Agreement defined Agent and exact account-holding legal entity on Bank's KYC/signature cards. Playbook requires three-party form; two-party acknowledgment is off-market and rejected.]

RECITALS

A. The Debtor and certain affiliates are parties to that certain [Senior Secured Credit Agreement], dated as of [________ __], 20[__] (as amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement"), among the Debtor, the lenders from time to time party thereto, and the Secured Party.

B. Pursuant to the Credit Agreement and the other Collateral Documents, the Debtor has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Deposit Accounts described on Schedule A hereto (each, a "Deposit Account" and collectively, the "Deposit Accounts"), including all cash, checks, wire transfers, automated clearing house entries, and other items from time to time credited thereto, and all proceeds thereof (collectively, the "Account Collateral").

C. The parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party's security interest in the Account Collateral by "control" within the meaning of Sections 9-104 and 9-314 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of [New York] (the "UCC"), and to set forth the Bank's agreements with respect to the Deposit Accounts.

[INSERT: D. This Agreement is a "Collateral Document" and a "Loan Document" under the Credit Agreement. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings assigned in the Credit Agreement. To the extent of any conflict between this Agreement and the Credit Agreement regarding the rights of the Secured Party against the Debtor, the Credit Agreement controls as between those parties; nothing in the Credit Agreement impairs the Bank's rights expressly set forth herein.]

AGREEMENT

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 Defined Terms. As used herein:

"Account Collateral" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals.

"Bankruptcy Code" means Title 11 of the United States Code.

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or day on which banks in [New York, New York] [or the city of the Bank's depositary operations] are authorized or required by law to close.

"Control Notice" [RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A (or other written instruction that the Bank can identify as originating from the Secured Party) directing that the Bank no longer comply with instructions originated by the Debtor and thereafter comply solely with instructions originated by the Secured Party with respect to the Deposit Accounts and Account Collateral.]
[DELETE: means any notice the Bank in good faith believes is from the Secured Party.]
[COMMENT: Counterparty's diluted definition undermines audit trail and playbook requirement for authenticated exclusive-control trigger.]

"Credit Agreement" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals.

"Deposit Accounts" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals and are more particularly described on Schedule A, as Schedule A may be updated by written notice from the Debtor and the Secured Party to the Bank.

"Excluded Account" means any deposit account exclusively used for (i) payroll, (ii) employee benefits in the ordinary course, (iii) tax withholding, or (iv) zero-balance accounts swept daily into a Deposit Account subject to this Agreement, in each case only to the extent and for so long as the Credit Agreement permits such exclusion; [INSERT: provided that no account holding collections of Receivables or other Collateral proceeds shall be an Excluded Account].

"Indemnified Liabilities" has the meaning set forth in Section 8.1.

"Instructions" means entitlement orders, payment orders, withdrawal requests, fund-transfer instructions, and other directions with respect to the Deposit Accounts or Account Collateral.

"Lien" means any mortgage, pledge, hypothecation, assignment, deposit arrangement, encumbrance, lien (statutory or other), charge, or preference, priority or other security interest or preferential arrangement of any kind or nature whatsoever.

[RESTORE-PLAYBOOK:
"Material Adverse Effect" means a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, properties, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Debtor and its subsidiaries, taken as a whole, (b) the ability of the Debtor to perform its obligations under this Agreement or any other Loan Document, (c) the legality, validity, binding effect, or enforceability of this Agreement or any other Loan Document, or (d) the rights of or benefits available to the Secured Party or the Secured Parties under this Agreement or any other Loan Document; provided that, for the avoidance of doubt, [DELETE: none of the following shall constitute or be taken into account in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred or would reasonably be expected to occur: (i) any regulatory action, investigation, consent order, fine, penalty, or supervisory directive by any Governmental Authority (including bank regulatory, consumer financial, or deposit-insurance authorities) relating to deposit accounts, cash management, BSA/AML, sanctions, or similar matters; (ii) any change in law, regulation, or supervisory guidance applicable to depository institutions or secured lending generally; or (iii) any action taken by the Bank to comply with Applicable Law]] [INSERT: the foregoing clauses (a)–(d) shall be construed consistently with the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" in the Credit Agreement, and no carve-out in this Agreement shall narrow Credit Agreement MAE or excuse any Debtor representation, covenant, or default standard herein. Regulatory, supervisory, BSA/AML, sanctions, or deposit-related actions or changes shall NOT be carved out of MAE for purposes of this Agreement.]
]
[COMMENT: CRITICAL DEVIATION. Counterparty added MAE carve-outs for regulatory action of the precise type at issue in this collateral package. Restore Credit Agreement-aligned MAE; delete regulatory carve-outs. See Issues/Risk Memo Issue 2.]

"Obligations" means all obligations of the Debtor to the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement, the other Loan Documents, and this Agreement, whether for principal, interest, fees, expenses, indemnities, or otherwise, including obligations arising after commencement of any Insolvency Proceeding (including interest accruing after such commencement).

"Person" means any natural person, corporation, limited liability company, trust, joint venture, association, company, partnership, Governmental Authority, or other entity.

"Secured Parties" has the meaning assigned in the Credit Agreement.

"UCC" has the meaning set forth in the Recitals. References to Division or Article 9 include corresponding provisions of the UCC as in effect in any relevant jurisdiction.

1.2 UCC Terms. "Account debtor," "authenticate," "control," "deposit account," "entitlement order," "proceeds," and other UCC terms used but not defined herein have the meanings assigned in the UCC.

1.3 Rules of Construction. The words "include," "includes," and "including" are deemed to be followed by "without limitation." References to Sections, Schedules, and Exhibits are to this Agreement unless otherwise indicated. Headings are for convenience only.

SECTION 2. THE DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS; CONTROL

2.1 Identification of Deposit Accounts. The Bank confirms that (a) the Debtor is the Bank's customer with respect to each Deposit Account, (b) each Deposit Account is a "deposit account" as defined in UCC § 9-102, (c) Schedule A correctly identifies each Deposit Account by account number and title as of the Effective Date, and (d) [INSERT: the Bank has not entered into any other control agreement, acknowledgment, or similar arrangement with respect to any Deposit Account in favor of any Person other than the Secured Party, except as expressly disclosed on Schedule A].

2.2 Establishment of Control (UCC § 9-104). The Bank agrees that it will comply with Instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Deposit Accounts without further consent by the Debtor. The parties acknowledge that this Agreement is intended to, and does, give the Secured Party "control" of each Deposit Account under UCC § 9-104(a)(2). [INSERT: The Bank subordinates any security interest, right of recoupment (other than as expressly preserved in Section 5), or other claim it may have in the Deposit Accounts to the security interest of the Secured Party, except for the Bank's set-off and recoupment rights expressly preserved in Section 5.2.]

2.3 Pre-Control Notice Mechanics; Standing Instructions.
(a) Until the Bank receives a Control Notice from the Secured Party, the Bank may comply with Instructions originated by the Debtor with respect to the Deposit Accounts, subject to Section 5 and ordinary Bank account documentation.
(b) [RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: Notwithstanding clause (a), the Debtor and the Secured Party may jointly deliver standing Instructions (including sweep, lockbox, concentration, and blocked-account Instructions) that the Bank shall implement and that the Debtor may not unilaterally revoke or amend without the Secured Party's prior written consent.]
(c) [INSERT: The Debtor shall not close, change the title of, or permit any Person other than the Debtor and the Secured Party to be authorized on, any Deposit Account without the Secured Party's prior written consent, and the Bank shall not honor any such request without confirmation of that consent.]

2.4 Exclusive Control After Control Notice.
(a) Upon the Bank's receipt of a Control Notice, the Bank shall (i) promptly confirm receipt in writing to the Secured Party and the Debtor, (ii) cease complying with Debtor-originated Instructions (other than Instructions to post credits and ordinary bank charges consistent with Section 5), and (iii) comply solely with Instructions originated by the Secured Party concerning the Deposit Accounts and Account Collateral.
(b) [RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: The Bank shall have no duty to inquire into the Secured Party's right to issue a Control Notice or any Instruction, or whether an Event of Default or other condition under the Credit Agreement exists, and the Bank may conclusively rely on any Control Notice or Instruction that the Bank reasonably believes to be genuine and authorized.]
(c) [INSERT: The Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to implement a Control Notice not later than the close of business on the Business Day of receipt if received before [12:00 p.m.] [Bank location] time, and otherwise by the close of the next Business Day.]
(d) [DELETE: The Bank may delay implementation of any Control Notice for up to five (5) Business Days to verify authenticity or to obtain internal approvals.]
[COMMENT: Multi-day unilateral delay is off-market and defeats emergency control; replace with same-day/next-day commercially reasonable efforts standard aligned to bank form and playbook.]

2.5 No Dual Control; Priority. The Bank will not enter into any agreement with any Person by which the Bank would be obligated to comply with Instructions concerning any Deposit Account originated by a Person other than the Debtor (prior to Control Notice) or the Secured Party (at any time). The Bank confirms that the Secured Party's security interest and control have priority over any Lien or claim of the Bank except as expressly set forth in Section 5.

2.6 Statements; Information Access. The Bank shall send copies of periodic account statements and, upon request of the Secured Party, [INSERT: promptly provide the Secured Party with online view access (read-only) and such other information regarding balances, transactions, and items as the Secured Party may reasonably request], in each case without further Debtor consent. [INSERT: Debtor hereby authorizes such disclosure and irrevocably instructs the Bank to comply.]

SECTION 3. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

3.1 Debtor Representations. The Debtor represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank, on the Effective Date and [RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: on each date on which any Account Collateral is credited to a Deposit Account], that:
(a) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization;
(b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and has taken all necessary organizational action to authorize the same;
(c) this Agreement constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy and equitable principles;
(d) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with its organizational documents, any material agreement binding upon it, or any law or order applicable to it, except for conflicts that would not reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect [RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: as defined herein without regulatory carve-outs];
(e) it is the sole owner of each Deposit Account free and clear of Liens other than Liens permitted under the Credit Agreement and the Bank's rights under Section 5;
(f) Schedule A is true, complete, and correct; and
(g) [INSERT: no Excluded Account holds collections of Collateral or other proceeds required by the Credit Agreement to be deposited into a controlled Deposit Account].

3.2 Bank Representations. The Bank represents and warrants that:
(a) it is a [national banking association / state bank] duly organized and validly existing;
(b) it has the power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement;
(c) this Agreement has been duly authorized, executed, and delivered and constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable against it subject to bankruptcy and equitable principles; and
(d) [INSERT: the officer executing this Agreement is authorized to bind the Bank with respect to deposit-account control arrangements of this type].

3.3 Survival of Representations.
[RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: The representations and warranties in this Section 3 shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement, the establishment of control, and any Control Notice, and shall survive termination of this Agreement solely as to claims arising from facts existing prior to termination, [DELETE: for a period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date] [INSERT: until the date that is the later of (i) full and indefeasible payment of the Obligations and termination of commitments under the Credit Agreement and (ii) three (3) years after termination of this Agreement (or for fraud or intentional misrepresentation, without limitation of time)], subject to any longer period required for claims relating to priority, control perfection, or Bank set-off disputes.]
]
[COMMENT: CRITICAL DEVIATION. Counterparty inserted a shortened limitation/survival period for core representations. Restore long-form survival aligned to Credit Agreement collateral package and playbook. See Issues/Risk Memo Issue 3.]

SECTION 4. COVENANTS

4.1 Debtor Covenants. The Debtor covenants that it shall:
(a) maintain each Deposit Account in existence and at the Bank unless the Secured Party consents in writing to transfer (and a replacement control agreement is in effect);
(b) deposit and cause to be deposited all proceeds of Collateral required by the Credit Agreement into Deposit Accounts subject to this Agreement (or another control agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Secured Party);
(c) not permit any Deposit Account to become subject to any control agreement or Lien in favor of any Person other than the Secured Party and the Bank (to the extent of Section 5);
(d) not change the account number or title of any Deposit Account without prior written notice to and consent of the Secured Party and prompt update of Schedule A;
(e) [INSERT: provide the Secured Party not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice before opening any new deposit account that is required by the Credit Agreement to be subject to control, and execute a joinder or replacement control agreement]; and
(f) [INSERT: not assert any claim against the Bank for complying with Instructions of the Secured Party or with this Agreement].

4.2 Bank Covenants. The Bank shall:
(a) not change its name, jurisdiction of organization, or the office at which the Deposit Accounts are maintained in a manner that would impair control perfection without prior written notice to the Secured Party;
(b) [INSERT: maintain ordinary-course books and records identifying the Deposit Accounts and this Agreement]; and
(c) upon reasonable request, confirm in writing to the Secured Party the balance of each Deposit Account and that this Agreement remains in full force and effect.

SECTION 5. BANK'S RIGHTS; SUBORDINATION; FEES

5.1 Account Documentation. This Agreement supplements, and in the event of conflict concerning control and priority controls over, the Bank's standard deposit-account agreements, cash-management terms, and signature cards (the "Bank Account Documents"). [INSERT: As between the Debtor and the Secured Party, nothing in the Bank Account Documents limits the Debtor's Obligations or the Secured Party's rights under the Loan Documents.]

5.2 Permitted Bank Set-Off and Charges. The Bank may charge the Deposit Accounts for:
(a) its customary fees and charges for maintaining the Deposit Accounts and providing cash-management services;
(b) the face amount of returned items, corrections, and adjustments in accordance with Applicable Law and Bank Account Documents; and
(c) [RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: obligations owed to the Bank solely in its capacity as depository bank with respect to the Deposit Accounts (including overdrafts on the Deposit Accounts)], 
[DELETE: any and all obligations of the Debtor to the Bank whether or not related to the Deposit Accounts, including loan, swap, and other credit exposures on a right-of-setoff basis superior to the Secured Party].
[COMMENT: Broad cross-affiliate set-off priority is off-market relative to firm playbook and standard bank form negotiated position; limit to account-related charges and returned items unless Credit Agreement expressly permits a capped returned-item reserve.]

5.3 Subordination. The Bank subordinates any Lien, right of set-off (other than Section 5.2), recoupment, or banker’s lien it may have in the Account Collateral to the perfected security interest and control of the Secured Party. This subordination is for perfection and priority only and does not create duties running from the Bank to lenders other than as expressly stated.

5.4 Fees. Debtor shall pay the Bank's and, [INSERT: to the extent provided in the Credit Agreement, the Secured Party's] reasonable fees and expenses in connection with this Agreement, including negotiation, amendments, and enforcement. [INSERT: Unpaid Bank fees may be charged to the Deposit Accounts pursuant to Section 5.2(a) but shall not prime the Secured Party's Lien as to other Account Collateral beyond ordinary monthly service charges and returned items.]

SECTION 6. INSTRUCTIONS; RELIANCE; LIMITATION OF BANK DUTIES

6.1 Authorized Secured Party Representatives. The Secured Party shall deliver to the Bank a list of authorized officers or a callback protocol. The Bank may rely on the most recent list or protocol received.

6.2 Limited Duties of Bank. The Bank undertakes only those duties expressly set forth herein. The Bank is not a fiduciary for the Debtor or the Secured Party. The Bank has no duty to monitor compliance by Debtor or Secured Party with the Credit Agreement or to determine whether an Event of Default exists.

6.3 Reliance. The Bank may rely on communications it reasonably believes to be genuine and authorized, and on advice of counsel.

SECTION 7. DEFAULT; REMEDIES INTEGRATION

7.1 Effect of Credit Agreement Default. An Event of Default under the Credit Agreement constitutes a default under this Agreement as between Debtor and Secured Party. The Bank's sole operational obligation upon Control Notice remains as set forth in Section 2.4, without independent default determination.

7.2 Rights Cumulative. Secured Party rights under this Agreement are cumulative with Loan Document remedies and UCC rights.

SECTION 8. INDEMNIFICATION; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

8.1 Debtor Indemnity of Bank and Secured Party.
The Debtor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Bank and the Secured Party, and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents (each, an "Indemnified Person"), from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys' fees and expenses) (collectively, "Indemnified Liabilities") arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Deposit Accounts, the Account Collateral, any Instruction, any Control Notice, or any action taken or omitted by an Indemnified Person in accordance herewith, [RESTORE-PLAYBOOK: EXCEPT to the extent finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction to have resulted primarily from such Indemnified Person's gross negligence or willful misconduct].
[DELETE: except to the extent arising from the Indemnified Person's negligence (whether sole, concurrent, or contributory).]

8.2 Indemnification Cap and Basket — REQUIRED RESTORATION.
[DELETE: The Debtor's aggregate liability under Section 8.1 shall not exceed $[_____] (the "Indemnity Cap"), and the Debtor shall have no liability for Indemnified Liabilities until the aggregate amount thereof exceeds $[_____] (the "Basket"), after which the Debtor shall be liable only for amounts in excess of the Basket (deductible).]
[DELETE / REJECT COUNTERPARTY SILENT CHANGE: any reduction of the Indemnity Cap below the playbook floor and any conversion of the Basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket.]
[RESTORE-PLAYBOOK / INSERT:
(a) Cap. The Debtor's aggregate liability to the Bank under Section 8.1 shall not exceed the greater of (i) $[PLAYBOOK FLOOR — restore firm standard / Credit Agreement indemnity economics; typically uncapped as to Debtor indemnity of Agent for collateral enforcement, or not less than the aggregate principal Commitments] and (ii) the aggregate amount of Obligations outstanding at any time of determination; provided that there shall be NO CAP on Indemnified Liabilities arising from (A) Debtor's fraud or willful misconduct, (B) Debtor's failure to pay Bank fees and returned items under Section 5, (C) third-party claims asserting priority contests caused by Debtor Liens or competing control agreements, or (D) Debtor breach of Sections 2.3, 3.1, or 4.1.
(b) Basket. [RESTORE: deductible, not tipping.] Debtor shall not be liable for Indemnified Liabilities under Section 8.1 until the aggregate amount of otherwise indemnifiable Indemnified Liabilities exceeds $[PLAYBOOK DEDUCTIBLE], and then only for the excess over such deductible amount. For the avoidance of doubt, the Basket is a true deductible and does NOT "tip" to dollar-one once exceeded.
(c) No Cap as to Secured Party. Nothing in this Section 8.2 limits the Debtor's indemnity or reimbursement obligations to the Secured Party or Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement or other Loan Documents, which remain [uncapped / as set forth in the Credit Agreement].
(d) Order of Operations. Indemnity claims are determined without regard to any counterparty-proposed silent reduction. Any prior draft reducing the cap or converting the basket to a tipping basket is rejected in full.
]
[COMMENT: CRITICAL DEVIATION. Counterparty silently reduced the indemnification cap and converted the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Both are unacceptable under the firm ACA playbook and inconsistent with Credit Agreement indemnity architecture. See Issues/Risk Memo Issue 1.]

8.3 Bank Limitation of Liability. The Bank shall not be liable for any special, indirect, consequential, or punitive damages. The Bank's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed [the amount of fees paid to the Bank hereunder in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim], except to the extent caused by the Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct as finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction. [INSERT: Nothing in this Section 8.3 impairs the Secured Party's perfected security interest, control, or priority, or the Bank's subordination undertakings in Section 5.3.]

8.4 Secured Party Liability. Neither the Secured Party nor any Secured Party shall have any liability to the Bank or Debtor under this Agreement except for its own gross negligence or willful misconduct as finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction, and then only for direct damages.

SECTION 9. TERM; TERMINATION; RELEASE

9.1 Term. This Agreement remains in effect until terminated in accordance with this Section 9.

9.2 Termination by Secured Party. The Secured Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice to the Bank and the Debtor following [INSERT: indefeasible payment in full of the Obligations and termination of Commitments, or release of the Deposit Accounts in accordance with the Credit Agreement].

9.3 Termination Mechanics. Upon termination, the Bank shall have no further obligations hereunder other than to comply with Debtor Instructions (subject to Bank Account Documents) and surviving provisions. [INSERT: Termination does not require Debtor consent when directed by Secured Party upon authorized release.]

9.4 Survival. Sections 3.3, 5.3, 6, 8, 9.4, 10, and 11 survive termination.

SECTION 10. GOVERNING LAW; VENUE; JURY WAIVER; SERVICE

10.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of [New York], without regard to conflicts-of-law principles that would require application of another jurisdiction's law, [INSERT: except that perfection, the effect of perfection or nonperfection, and priority of security interests in the Deposit Accounts are governed by the local law of the Bank's jurisdiction under UCC § 9-304].

10.2 Venue; Submission to Jurisdiction. Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in [the Borough of Manhattan, New York City] [Bank form venue if required and playbook-accepted], and waives objections based on venue or forum non conveniens.

10.3 WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL. EACH PARTY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY.

10.4 Service of Process. Each party consents to service of process by overnight courier to the addresses in Section 11.

SECTION 11. MISCELLANEOUS

11.1 Amendments. No amendment or waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by the Debtor, the Secured Party, and the Bank (except that Schedule A may be updated as provided in Section 2.1 with notice to the Bank, and the Secured Party may unilaterally update authorized-officer lists).

11.2 Notices. All notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, overnight courier, or email (with confirmation) to the addresses set forth on Schedule B (or such other address as a party designates by notice). Control Notices shall be delivered pursuant to the Bank's notice requirements on Schedule B and are effective upon receipt (or as provided in Section 2.4).

11.3 Successors and Assigns; Secured Party Assignment. This Agreement binds and benefits the parties and their successors and permitted assigns. [INSERT: The Secured Party may assign or transfer its rights hereunder in connection with an assignment of its rights under the Credit Agreement without Bank or Debtor consent, upon written notice to the Bank; the Bank shall treat the assignee as Secured Party upon receipt of such notice and any reasonably required documentation.] Debtor may not assign without prior written consent of Secured Party and Bank.

11.4 Severability. If any provision is held invalid, the remainder continues in full force.

11.5 Counterparts; Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts (including PDF/electronic), each of which is an original, and all of which constitute one instrument. Electronic signatures are effective.

11.6 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with the Schedules and Exhibits and (as between Debtor and Secured Party) the Loan Documents, constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes prior agreements relating to control of the Deposit Accounts.

11.7 No Third-Party Beneficiaries. Except for Indemnified Persons and Secured Parties, there are no third-party beneficiaries.

11.8 Further Assurances. Each party shall execute and deliver such further documents and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate control perfection and the purposes of this Agreement. [INSERT: Debtor authorizes Secured Party to file UCC financing statements and amendments describing the Account Collateral.]

11.9 [INSERT: USA PATRIOT Act / KYC. Bank hereby notifies the parties that pursuant to the requirements of the USA PATRIOT Act, it is required to obtain, verify, and record information identifying the other parties. Debtor and Secured Party shall promptly provide information reasonably requested by Bank for BSA/AML compliance; provided that such process shall not delay effectiveness of control once this Agreement is executed.]

11.10 [INSERT: Force Majeure limited. Bank is not liable for failure to perform due to causes beyond its reasonable control, provided it gives prompt notice and resumes performance as soon as practicable; force majeure does not excuse subordination or the obligation to implement Control Notices once systems are operational.]

SECTION 12. [INSERT: CREDIT AGREEMENT INTEGRATION AND CONFLICTS]

[INSERT:
12.1 Loan Document Status. This Agreement is a Loan Document. Debtor's breach of this Agreement is a breach of the Credit Agreement (subject to any applicable grace or notice provisions therein solely as between Debtor and Secured Parties).
12.2 Conflicts. As between Debtor and Secured Party, if this Agreement conflicts with the Credit Agreement or Collateral Documents regarding Obligations, Events of Default, or release standards, the Credit Agreement and Collateral Documents control. As among the parties with respect to the Bank's duties, control mechanics, fees, and Section 5 rights, this Agreement controls.
12.3 Agency. The Secured Party acts under this Agreement in its agency capacity under the Credit Agreement; it may exercise rights hereunder based on instructions from Required Lenders or as otherwise permitted by the Credit Agreement, and shall not be liable for actions taken in accordance therewith except for gross negligence or willful misconduct.
]

SCHEDULE A — Deposit Accounts
[INSERT complete account details from account schedule / Bank checklist:]
Bank Name: [DEPOSITORY BANK]
Bank ABA/Routing: [________]
Branch / Office Location (UCC § 9-304 jurisdiction): [________]
Account Title: [________]
Account Number: [________]
Account Type: [operating / concentration / lockbox / collections]
Excluded Account? [Yes/No — if Yes, basis under Credit Agreement]
Existing Competing Control Agreements: [None / describe]

[COMMENT: Reconcile every line against (1) Credit Agreement collateral schedule, (2) Bank standard form account listing, (3) correspondence confirming open accounts and authorized signers. Missing account numbers or wrong legal title = perfection defect.]

SCHEDULE B — Notice Addresses and Control Notice Delivery Protocol
Debtor: [address; email; attention]
Secured Party: [address; email; attention; after-hours contact for Control Notice]
Bank: [address; email; authenticated portal / callback protocol; attention of Deposit Operations / Control Agreements desk]

EXHIBIT A — Form of Control Notice
[RESTORE-PLAYBOOK standard form:]
Date: ________
To: [Bank] — Deposit Account Control Desk
Re: Control Notice — Account Control Agreement dated [●] among [Debtor], [Secured Party], and [Bank]

Ladies and Gentlemen:
Pursuant to Section 2 of the above-referenced Account Control Agreement, the undersigned Secured Party hereby delivers this Control Notice and instructs you to (i) cease complying with instructions originated by the Debtor with respect to the Deposit Accounts listed on Schedule A thereto and (ii) comply solely with instructions originated by the Secured Party.
Authorized signature: ________________________
Name/Title: _________________________________
Callback phone: _____________________________

EXHIBIT B — [INSERT: Authorized Officers of Secured Party / Callback Protocol]

================================================================================
END OF REDLINE — SUMMARY OF PRINCIPAL REQUIRED MODIFICATIONS
================================================================================

1. INDEMNITY CAP & BASKET (Section 8.2): Reject silent cap reduction; restore playbook floor / Credit Agreement-aligned economics; restore true DEDUCTIBLE basket (reject tipping basket); preserve uncapped categories (fraud, priority contests, fee/returned-item obligations, specified covenant breaches); no cap on Debtor indemnity of Secured Party under Loan Documents.

2. MAE DEFINITION (Section 1.1): Delete counterparty regulatory-action carve-outs; align MAE to Credit Agreement; expressly state regulatory/BSA-AML/sanctions/deposit-related matters are NOT carved out.

3. SURVIVAL / LIMITATION PERIOD (Section 3.3): Delete shortened survival for core representations; restore survival through indefeasible payment plus residual tail (and unlimited for fraud); preserve survival for priority/control/set-off disputes.

4. CONTROL NOTICE MECHANICS (Sections 1.1, 2.4): Restore authenticated form of Control Notice; delete multi-day unilateral Bank delay; insert same-day/next-day commercially reasonable implementation standard.

5. BANK SET-OFF (Section 5.2): Narrow broad cross-product superior set-off to account-related fees, returned items, and depositary overdrafts on the controlled accounts.

6. PERFECTION / PRIORITY PROTECTIONS (Sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 5.3): Insert no-competing-control confirmation, subordination language, and anti-dual-control covenant.

7. INFORMATION RIGHTS (Section 2.6): Insert Secured Party view access and statement delivery without further Debtor consent.

8. NEW ACCOUNTS / JOINDER (Section 4.1): Insert notice and replacement control-agreement covenant for newly opened accounts required to be controlled.

9. CREDIT AGREEMENT INTEGRATION (Recital D; Section 12): Insert Loan Document status, conflict rule, and agency reliance.

10. UCC § 9-304 / GOVERNING LAW (Section 10.1): Insert local-law perfection rule for deposit accounts; preserve NY contract law and jury waiver.

11. ASSIGNMENT (Section 11.3): Permit Secured Party assignment with notice in connection with Credit Agreement assignments.

12. SCHEDULE A / ACCOUNT DETAILS: Complete and verify against Bank form, Credit Agreement schedules, and correspondence; cure any title/number mismatches before signing.

[COMMENT: All modifications above are required for playbook compliance, Credit Agreement consistency, and enforceable UCC control. See companion issues-risk-memo.docx for deviation-by-deviation risk ratings, exposure analysis, recommended fallback positions, and summary deviation matrix.]

args.title: issues-risk-memo.docx
args.body:
ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review

TO:      Client Working Group; File
FROM:    Contracts / Banking Counsel
DATE:    [Engagement Date]
RE:      Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement — Deviations, Missing Protections, Off-Market Terms, Risk Ratings, and Recommended Positions
MATTER:  Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
RELATED: aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline incorporating all required modifications)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("ACA" or "Agreement") against: (i) the firm internal ACA playbook; (ii) the executed Senior Secured Credit Agreement and related Collateral Documents; (iii) the depository bank's standard form control agreement; (iv) the account schedule and account-opening details; and (v) related correspondence and closing checklists.

The counterparty draft accepts a substantial portion of firm-standard architecture (three-party control structure, pre-/post-notice instruction framework, Bank limited-duty posture). However, it introduces three material, intentional deviations that must be rejected or tightly cabined, and it omits several market-standard secured-party protections required for UCC Article 9 control perfection, priority, and Credit Agreement integration.

Primary counterparty deviations (from counterparty markup file):
  (1) Indemnification cap silently reduced; basket converted from deductible to tipping basket;
  (2) Material Adverse Effect definition expanded with regulatory-action carve-outs of the type directly relevant to this deposit/cash-management collateral package;
  (3) New limitation period shortens survival of core representations.

In addition, relative to playbook, Credit Agreement, and bank standard form, the draft is deficient on Control Notice authentication and timing, Bank set-off breadth, competing-control representations, Secured Party information rights, new-account joinder, Loan Document integration, UCC § 9-304 governing-law precision, and assignment mechanics.

Recommendation: Do not execute the counterparty draft as proposed. Circulate aca-redline.docx as the working mark. Treat Issues 1–3 as HIGH and non-waivable without Credit Committee / partner sign-off and express Credit Agreement consistency analysis. Remaining issues are MEDIUM or LOW but should be cleared before signing to avoid perfection, priority, or operational gaps.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. REVIEW STANDARD AND MATERIALS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A. Materials Reviewed
  1. Deal materials — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (Matter File 6)
  2. Counterparty markup — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
  3. Firm ACA Playbook requirements (control perfection; exclusive control on notice; indemnity architecture; MAE alignment; survival; Bank set-off limits; integration with Credit Agreement)
  4. Executed Credit Agreement standards (Loan Document status; Obligations; Events of Default; MAE; indefeasible payment / release; agency)
  5. Depository bank standard form (Control Notice mechanics; limited Bank duties; customary fees/returned items; KYC)
  6. Account details / Schedule expectations and related correspondence/checklists

B. Legal Framework
  • UCC §§ 9-104 (control of deposit accounts), 9-304 (location of bank / local law for perfection and priority), 9-314 (perfection by control), 9-327 (priority of security interests in deposit accounts), 9-340/9-341 (bank's rights / reciprocal)
  • Credit Agreement Collateral Document and Loan Document definitions
  • Market practice for three-party ACAs among institutional lenders, borrowers, and cash-management banks

C. Risk Rating Key
  HIGH     — Material adverse effect on perfection, priority, recoveries, or Credit Agreement economics; reject or require playbook restoration
  MEDIUM   — Meaningful commercial or operational risk; negotiate to playbook; limited fallback possible with mitigants
  LOW      — Cleanup, consistency, or preference; accept only with documentation of rationale

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. CRITICAL COUNTERPARTY DEVIATIONS (MARKUP-FLAGGED)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced; Basket Converted to Tipping Basket
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 8.1 (indemnity grant); § 8.2 (cap and basket)
Playbook Requirement:     Debtor indemnity of Bank and Secured Party with (a) cap no lower than playbook floor / Credit Agreement indemnity economics (and uncapped categories for fraud, priority contests, fee/returned-item obligations, and specified covenant breaches); (b) true DEDUCTIBLE basket (Debtor pays only excess over basket); (c) no cap on Debtor indemnity/reimbursement of Secured Party under the Credit Agreement; (d) exclusion standard of gross negligence/willful misconduct (final court determination), not simple negligence.
Counterparty Position:    Silently reduces the indemnification cap below playbook/Credit Agreement floor; converts basket from deductible to tipping basket (once basket exceeded, liability runs from dollar-one); softens conduct exception toward ordinary negligence in places.
Deviation Type:           Economic term change + structural change to loss-sharing; off-market relative to secured lending collateral packages; inconsistent with Credit Agreement indemnity architecture.
Risk Rating:              HIGH
Exposure Analysis:        A reduced cap truncates recoveries for Bank operational claims and third-party priority contests that the Debtor is in the best position to prevent (competing Liens, misdirected proceeds, unauthorized account changes). A tipping basket increases Debtor (and indirectly estate) exposure volatility and is often used to re-characterize ordinary deductible economics; once tipped, small claims aggregate into full dollar-one indemnity, altering settlement leverage and reserve expectations. If Bank liability or third-party claims exceed the silent cap during enforcement or insolvency, residual risk shifts to Secured Party recoveries on Account Collateral or creates Bank friction on honoring Control Notices. Misalignment with uncapped or higher Credit Agreement indemnities creates interpretive conflicts and estoppel arguments that ACA indemnity is the exclusive measure.
Recommended Position:     REJECT silent cap reduction and REJECT tipping basket. Restore: (i) playbook floor / greater-of floor tied to Obligations or Commitments as applicable; (ii) true deductible basket; (iii) express uncapped categories (fraud/willful misconduct of Debtor; Bank fees and returned items; third-party priority contests from Debtor Liens or competing control agreements; breaches of §§ 2.3, 3.1, 4.1); (iv) no limitation on Credit Agreement indemnity to Secured Parties; (v) gross negligence/willful misconduct (final judicial determination) as the sole Bank/Secured Party conduct carve-out. Fallback (partner approval required): modest cap reduction only if still ≥ playbook absolute floor AND deductible basket retained AND uncapped categories preserved AND Credit Agreement indemnity expressly untouched.
Redline Treatment:        See aca-redline.docx § 8.2 — full restoration language; deletion of counterparty cap/basket formulation.
Negotiation Points:       - Demand blackline showing prior cap figure vs. silent reduction
                          - Confirm basket arithmetic examples (deductible vs. tip)
                          - Align with Credit Agreement § indemnity cross-reference

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 2 — Material Adverse Effect Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 1.1 (definition of Material Adverse Effect); cross-refs in § 3.1(d) and any MAE-triggered covenants/conditions
Playbook Requirement:     MAE must align with Credit Agreement MAE. No ACA-specific carve-outs that narrow Credit Agreement standards. Regulatory, supervisory, BSA/AML, sanctions, consumer-financial, or deposit-insurance actions and related changes in law/guidance must NOT be carved out of MAE for ACA purposes where MAE gates representations, conflicts, or Debtor performance standards.
Counterparty Position:    Adds carve-outs excluding from MAE: (i) regulatory action, investigation, consent order, fine, penalty, or supervisory directive by Governmental Authorities (including bank regulatory, consumer financial, or deposit-insurance authorities) relating to deposit accounts, cash management, BSA/AML, sanctions, or similar matters; (ii) changes in law/regulation/supervisory guidance applicable to depository institutions or secured lending generally; (iii) Bank actions to comply with Applicable Law.
Deviation Type:           Definitional narrowing of a core risk allocation term; off-market in secured-party ACA paper when regulatory risk is precisely the operational context of deposit control; creates Credit Agreement inconsistency.
Risk Rating:              HIGH
Exposure Analysis:        The carve-outs match "exactly the kind" of regulatory action relevant to controlled deposit accounts and cash management. If a regulatory event impairs Debtor's ability to maintain accounts, causes forced account migration, freezes, or consent-order restrictions on dispositions, or undermines enforceability/operations of control arrangements, Debtor could argue no MAE—and therefore no breach of MAE-qualified representations or covenants—despite material collateral impairment. Divergent MAE between ACA and Credit Agreement invites selective invocation and weakens Event of Default / enforcement narratives. Carve-out (iii) regarding Bank legal compliance is unnecessary (Bank already has limited duties and legal-compliance protections elsewhere) and could be misread to sanitize Debtor-side impacts.
Recommended Position:     DELETE all three regulatory carve-outs. Define MAE by express cross-reference to, or substantive alignment with, Credit Agreement MAE, plus ACA-specific prongs for enforceability of the ACA and rights/benefits of Secured Party. State expressly that regulatory/BSA-AML/sanctions/deposit-related actions are not carved out. Fallback: if Bank insists on comfort that its own legally required actions are not a Bank default, place that solely in Bank limitation-of-liability / force majeure sections—not in MAE.
Redline Treatment:        See aca-redline.docx § 1.1 Material Adverse Effect — deletion of carve-outs; restoration of Credit Agreement-aligned definition.
Negotiation Points:       - Walk counterparties through why deposit-regulatory carve-outs are deal-specific risk shifting
                          - Offer Bank-side compliance safe harbor outside MAE
                          - Require identical MAE text or incorporation by reference to Credit Agreement

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 3 — Shortened Survival / Limitation Period for Core Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 3.3 (survival of representations); related claims under §§ 3.1, 3.2, 8
Playbook Requirement:     Core representations (organization, authority, enforceability, ownership of accounts, absence of competing control, Schedule A accuracy) survive execution, establishment of control, and Control Notice; survive termination as to pre-termination facts through at least indefeasible payment of Obligations plus a residual tail (playbook: later of payment-in-full/termination of commitments and three (3) years post-termination); fraud/intentional misrepresentation unlimited; claims regarding priority, control perfection, and Bank set-off disputes preserved for so long as relevant.
Counterparty Position:    Inserts a new limitation period shortening survival for core representations (counterparty markup: shortened survival; draft reflection includes a twelve (12) month from Effective Date formulation or similar truncated period).
Deviation Type:           Temporal limitation on fundamental collateral representations; off-market for perfection-critical reps; conflicts with long-dated credit facilities and post-default enforcement timelines.
Risk Rating:              HIGH
Exposure Analysis:        Control perfection and priority disputes often surface at enforcement, refinancing, amendment, or insolvency—frequently well after the first anniversary. A 12-month (or similarly short) survival extinguishes Debtor liability for misrepresented account ownership, undisclosed competing control agreements, or Schedule A errors discovered during workout. That shifts latent perfection defects onto Secured Parties and may leave Bank caught between competing claimants without Debtor indemnity support. Short survival also undercuts bring-down utility of reps that should reaffirm as Account Collateral is credited over the life of the facility.
Recommended Position:     DELETE shortened limitation period. Restore survival through later of (i) indefeasible payment in full of Obligations and termination of Commitments and (ii) three (3) years after ACA termination; unlimited for fraud/intentional misrepresentation; express preservation for priority/control/set-off disputes. Maintain bring-down of Debtor reps on each date Account Collateral is credited (or at least periodic bring-down consistent with Credit Agreement). Fallback: survival not less than the statute of limitations applicable to written contracts in the governing-law state for non-fraud reps, and never shorter than the scheduled Credit Agreement maturity plus two (2) years.
Redline Treatment:        See aca-redline.docx § 3.3 — full restoration of survival architecture.
Negotiation Points:       - Emphasize enforcement/insolvency discovery lag
                          - Distinguish Bank operational reps (may accept shorter) from Debtor ownership/control reps (must remain long-dated)
                          - Tie survival to Obligations discharge, not arbitrary anniversary of signing

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. ADDITIONAL DEVIATIONS, MISSING PROTECTIONS, AND OFF-MARKET TERMS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 4 — Control Notice Definition and Authentication Diluted
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 1.1 (Control Notice); § 2.4; Exhibit A
Playbook / Bank Form:     Control Notice must be written, identifiable as from Secured Party, preferably substantially in prescribed form with callback/authorized-officer protocol.
Counterparty/Draft Gap:   Diluted to any notice Bank "in good faith believes" is from Secured Party, without form or authentication protocol.
Risk Rating:              HIGH (operational / fraud / repudiation risk)
Exposure Analysis:        Weak authentication increases risk of fraudulent instructions and, conversely, Debtor challenges to legitimate notices. Undermines clean UCC control record.
Recommended Position:     Restore form Exhibit A + authorized-officer list/callback. Permit Bank good-faith reliance only on top of formal notice standards, not in lieu of them.
Redline:                  §§ 1.1, 2.4, Exhibit A, Exhibit B

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 5 — Multi-Day Bank Delay to Implement Control Notice
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 2.4
Playbook / Bank Form:     Same-day if received before cutoff; otherwise next Business Day; commercially reasonable efforts; no multi-business-day unilateral "verification" hold that defeats emergency control.
Counterparty/Draft Gap:   Up to five (5) Business Days to verify authenticity or obtain internal approvals.
Risk Rating:              HIGH
Exposure Analysis:        Five Business Days permits full dissipation of Account Collateral post-default. Inconsistent with purpose of exclusive control and with typical bank-form timing once callback is completed.
Recommended Position:     Delete 5-Business-Day delay. Insert same-day/next-day commercially reasonable efforts standard; authentication via pre-agreed callback, not open-ended delay.
Redline:                  § 2.4(c)–(d)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 6 — Overbroad Bank Set-Off / Cross-Product Priority
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 5.2
Playbook / Market:        Bank may charge customary account fees, returned items, and depositary overdrafts on the controlled accounts; broad superior set-off for unrelated loans, swaps, or affiliate exposures is off-market unless expressly negotiated and often capped.
Counterparty/Draft Gap:   Language permitting any and all Debtor obligations to Bank (including loan/swap/credit exposures) with set-off superior to Secured Party.
Risk Rating:              HIGH
Exposure Analysis:        Primes lender collateral with Bank's unrelated credit exposure; can hollow out controlled balances at enforcement; conflicts with UCC priority expectations negotiated in intercreditor/cash-dominion structures.
Recommended Position:     Limit § 5.2 to account fees, returned items/corrections, and overdrafts on the Deposit Accounts. Any broader Bank product set-off requires express Credit Agreement permission and should be capped and disclosed.
Redline:                  § 5.2

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 7 — Missing Competing-Control Representation and Anti-Dual-Control Covenant
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     §§ 2.1, 2.5, 3.1, 5.3
Playbook / UCC:           Bank confirmation of no other control agreement; covenant not to enter conflicting instruction agreements; subordination of Bank Liens other than permitted § 5.2 rights; Debtor rep of sole ownership free of competing control.
Risk Rating:              HIGH (perfection/priority)
Exposure Analysis:        Undisclosed second control agreement can destroy or dilute "control" priority under UCC § 9-327 and create instruction conflicts.
Recommended Position:     Insert Bank rep/confirm no competing control (Schedule A disclosure only); anti-dual-control covenant; Debtor ownership/Lien rep; express subordination.
Redline:                  §§ 2.1(d), 2.2, 2.5, 3.1(e), 5.3

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 8 — Secured Party Information and View-Access Rights Absent or Weak
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 2.6
Playbook:                 Automatic statement copies; read-only online access; balance/transaction info on request; Debtor authorization hardwired.
Risk Rating:              MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:        Without visibility, cash dominion, borrowing-base, and default monitoring degrade; delays detection of leakage.
Recommended Position:     Insert mandatory statements, view access, and irrevocable Debtor authorization for Bank disclosure to Secured Party.
Redline:                  § 2.6

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 9 — New Account Notice and Joinder / Replacement Control Covenant Missing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 4.1
Playbook / Credit Agreement: Advance notice before opening accounts required to be controlled; simultaneous joinder or new ACA.
Risk Rating:              MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:        Proceeds may land in uncontrolled accounts; springing perfection gaps; audit/checklist failures at closing and ongoing.
Recommended Position:     Insert ≥10 Business Days' prior notice and executed joinder/replacement before funding into new accounts (or hard grace consistent with Credit Agreement).
Redline:                  § 4.1(e)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 10 — Credit Agreement Integration / Loan Document Status Missing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     Recitals; new § 12; § 9 termination/release
Playbook / Credit Agreement: ACA is a Collateral Document and Loan Document; conflict rule; agency reliance; release only on indefeasible payment or permitted release; Debtor breach of ACA = Credit Agreement breach (subject to grace as applicable).
Risk Rating:              MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:        Without integration, disputes arise over whether ACA breach triggers facility default, whether Agent may rely on lender instructions, and whether release standards match the Credit Agreement.
Recommended Position:     Insert Recital D and § 12; align § 9 termination to indefeasible payment / Credit Agreement release mechanics.
Redline:                  Recital D; §§ 9.2, 12

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 11 — UCC § 9-304 Local-Law Perfection Rule Not Specified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 10.1
Playbook:                 Contract law = NY (or deal standard); perfection/effect/priority for deposit accounts = local law of Bank's jurisdiction (UCC § 9-304).
Risk Rating:              MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:        Ambiguous governing-law clause can complicate multi-state enforcement and opinion practice.
Recommended Position:     Split governing-law clause as in redline.
Redline:                  § 10.1

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 12 — Secured Party Assignment Mechanics Absent
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 11.3
Playbook:                 Secured Party may assign with Credit Agreement assignment upon notice to Bank; Bank to recognize assignee.
Risk Rating:              MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:        Agency succession, securitization warehouse transfers, or lender restructurings stall if Bank/Debtor consent is required.
Recommended Position:     Permit assignment on notice with reasonable KYC docs; no Debtor consent.
Redline:                  § 11.3

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 13 — Excluded Accounts Definition Permits Collateral Leakage
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 1.1 Excluded Account; § 3.1(g)
Playbook / Credit Agreement: Payroll/benefits/tax/ZBA exclusions only as Credit Agreement allows; no exclusion for receivables/collections accounts.
Risk Rating:              MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:        Mis-tagged "excluded" collections accounts defeat cash dominion.
Recommended Position:     Tighten definition; add Debtor rep that no Excluded Account holds Collateral collections.
Redline:                  §§ 1.1, 3.1(g)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 14 — Indemnity Conduct Standard Softened (Negligence vs. Gross Negligence)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     § 8.1
Playbook:                 Carve-out limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct finally determined by a court.
Counterparty Drift:       Ordinary negligence exception.
Risk Rating:              MEDIUM
Exposure Analysis:        Ordinary-negligence carve-out invites fact-intensive disputes and reduces practical value of Debtor indemnity to Bank during control implementation.
Recommended Position:     Restore gross negligence / willful misconduct + final judicial determination.
Redline:                  § 8.1

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 15 — Schedule A Account Details Incomplete / Unverified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     Schedule A; § 2.1; § 3.1(f)
Playbook / Checklist:     Exact legal title, account numbers, ABA, branch/office for UCC § 9-304, account type, competing-control disclosure, reconciliation to Credit Agreement collateral schedule and Bank KYC cards.
Risk Rating:              HIGH if inaccurate; MEDIUM as process item
Exposure Analysis:        Wrong account number or title = failure to establish control over intended accounts; classic closing defect.
Recommended Position:     Complete Schedule A from Bank checklist and Credit Agreement schedules before signing; bring-down confirmation at funding.
Redline:                  Schedule A structure and verification comment block

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 16 — Jury Waiver / Venue / Notices / Electronic Signatures (Cleanup)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     §§ 10.2–10.4, 11.2, 11.5
Playbook:                 Mutual jury waiver; NY federal/state exclusive venue (or bank-required venue if playbook-accepted); notice mechanics that make Control Notice receipt clear; electronic signatures permitted.
Risk Rating:              LOW to MEDIUM
Recommended Position:     Conform to playbook and bank form; ensure Control Notice delivery protocol is operationally tested.
Redline:                  §§ 10–11; Schedule B

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 17 — PATRIOT Act / KYC and Limited Force Majeure
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Agreement Section(s):     §§ 11.9, 11.10 (insertions)
Playbook / Bank Form:     Standard KYC notice; force majeure does not excuse subordination or post-restoration Control Notice implementation.
Risk Rating:              LOW
Recommended Position:     Accept standard KYC; cabin force majeure as in redline.
Redline:                  §§ 11.9, 11.10

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
V. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
